title: O Grieve Not So, nor So Lament
alsoKnownAs: Not So Darkly, Not So Deep
Why This Sad and Mournful Guise?
description: O Grieve Not So, nor So Lament in Tonic Solfa: the solfa line by line with the words, staff notation, all 5 verses, and a piano to sing along with.
about: The words are by Paul Gerhardt, first published in 1923. The English translation is by Sarah Laurie Findlater (nee Borthwick) (1854). The tune, ERFURT, is by Ludwig Herman Ilse (1910). This version of the melody and the words comes from the Open Hymnal Project.
underlay: O grieve not so, nor so la-ment, My soul! nor trou-bled sigh, Be-cause some joys to o-thers sent Your Fa-ther may de-ny; Take all as love that seems se-vere There is no want if God is near.

lines: O grieve not so, nor so lament,
My soul! nor troubled sigh,
Because some joys to others sent
Your Father may deny;
Take all as love that seems severe
There is no want if God is near.
There is no right you can demand,
No title you can claim;
For all are strangers in the land
Who bear the human name:
Earth and its treasures are the Lord's,
And He the lot of each accords.
How thankless art you, child of man!
For favors that abound;
Your God has giv'n you eyes to scan
The glory all around;
Yet seldom for this priceless sight,
Have you been heard to praise aright.
Number your limbs, your members tell,
And ask your thankless soul,
If to another you would sell
The smallest of them all.
There is not one from which your heart
Would willingly submit to part.
Now, go and search the depths of mind,
Explore its wondrous pow'r,
New proofs of benefits to find,
That meet you ev'ry hour;
More than the sand upon the shore,
And ever rising more and more.
